# Layout acceptance record {#sec-layout-acceptance}

This final layout chapter records what the Phase 2 checks prove and what still
requires human judgment. Its opening sentence is a fourth ordinary-chapter
marker for physical-page parity, independent of contents entries and displayed
folios.

## Automated evidence {#sec-automated-layout-evidence}

Every PDF must remain between thirty and fifty physical pages, use the declared
trim size, embed and subset the selected font faces, and retain the shared
structural markers. The validator locates unique prose on each ordinary chapter
and appendix opener and requires an odd physical page. It separately requires
the fixed front-matter verso to contain no extractable text, which catches
accidental folios and running titles as well as visible placeholder content.

The boundary corpus must place at least one labeled paragraph across a page in
every PDF profile. That assertion prevents a future layout change from turning
the widow/orphan fixture into a test that never reaches a boundary. LuaLaTeX
uses prohibitive widow, club, and display-widow penalties; Typst uses explicit
nonzero widow and orphan costs. HTML and EPUB declare two-line preferences for
reading systems that implement paged-media CSS.

Reflowable validation confirms that long chapter text survives in both HTML and
EPUB, internal links remain valid, the EPUB remains conforming, and the theme
contains heading overflow and paragraph boundary rules. It does not manufacture
recto sheets or blank pages where the medium has no stable facing-page model.

## Visual evidence {#sec-visual-layout-evidence}

A reviewer still inspects the 6 x 9 profiles first. The long chapter, section,
subsection, and detail headings must wrap inside the live area without losing
their number or separating from the following paragraph. Running furniture may
wrap compactly, but it must remain above its rule, avoid the folio, and leave the
body area untouched. At every labeled paragraph crossing, at least two lines
must remain on each side of the page break.

The same pages are then sampled at 7 x 10 and Letter sizes to confirm that wider
measures do not create a different hierarchy or an implausibly loose rhythm.
Typst and LuaLaTeX may choose different line breaks and page counts; the review
asks whether each composition is coherent, not whether the two are identical.

This division between automated invariants and concise visual review is the
Phase 2 handoff. It gives later authoring features a stable page system while
keeping aesthetic decisions visible and revisable.
